items.followUp: Why is Newton’s second law sometimes called the law of acceleration?

rubric.why: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist a change in its state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that inertia resists a change in rest or motion.

rubric.why: Newton’s first law describes the effect of inertia on an object’s motion.
rubric.description: Connects Newton’s first law to inertia.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the law is called the law of inertia because it describes inertia.

modelAnswer: Inertia is the tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of rest or uniform motion.
Newton’s first law describes this property of matter; therefore, it is known as the Law of Inertia.

items.followUp: Define acceleration and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Force is described as a push or pull.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining force as a push or pull that can change or tend to change motion.

rubric.why: The newton is the SI unit of force.
rubric.description: Names the SI unit of force.

modelAnswer: A force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion of a body.
The SI unit of force is the newton (N).

items.followUp: What is an Atwood machine, and how can it be used to study acceleration?

rubric.why: An Atwood machine has two masses connected by a string passing over a pulley.
rubric.description: Describes the construction of an Atwood machine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying two masses connected by a string over a pulley.

rubric.why: The machine can be used to determine the acceleration due to gravity.
rubric.description: Gives one use of the machine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid use, such as measuring g.

modelAnswer: An Atwood machine consists of two masses connected by a light string passing over a pulley.
It is used to determine the acceleration due to gravity, g.

items.followUp: Define gravitational field strength and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: A gravitational field is the region where a mass experiences gravitational force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the region around a mass in which another mass experiences gravitational force.

rubric.why: Gravitational field strength is force per unit mass at a point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or the relation g = F/m.

modelAnswer: A gravitational field is the region around a body in which another body experiences a gravitational force.
Gravitational field strength at a point is the gravitational force per unit mass placed at that point: g = F/m.

items.followUp: Define periodic motion and give two examples.

rubric.why: Random motion is irregular and does not follow a fixed direction or path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the motion is irregular or changes direction randomly.

rubric.why: These are examples of objects that undergo random motion.
rubric.description: Gives two examples of random motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid examples.

modelAnswer: Random motion is motion in which an object moves irregularly, changing direction without following a fixed path.
Examples include the motion of gas molecules and dust particles in air.

items.followUp: What is one use of a radar gun?

rubric.why: A LIDAR gun is used to detect the speed of a moving vehicle.
rubric.description: Identifies the quantity measured and the object measured.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it measures vehicle speed.

rubric.why: The gun uses laser light to make its measurement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning laser light or pulses used to measure the vehicle’s speed.

modelAnswer: A LIDAR gun uses laser pulses to measure the speed of a moving vehicle.
It is commonly used by traffic police to detect speeding vehicles.

items.followUp: What is atmospheric pressure, and why does it act on objects?

rubric.why: The atmosphere exerts pressure because air has weight.
rubric.description: States the cause of atmospheric pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking atmospheric pressure to the weight of air.

rubric.why: Atmospheric pressure acts on bodies from all directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that air pressure acts in all directions.

modelAnswer: The atmosphere exerts pressure on objects because the air has weight.
Atmospheric pressure acts on bodies in all directions.
